targeted_profiles.title: Elderly with Sepsis and High Vasopressor Use
targeted_profiles.clinical_story: An 85-year-old male with long-standing hypertension and diabetes presents with septic shock requiring high-dose norepinephrine and epinephrine infusions. Despite aggressive ICU care including Foley catheterization for fluid monitoring, he develops multi-organ dysfunction and ultimately succumbs to refractory shock.
targeted_profiles.why_this_profile: This profile targets patients with high mortality risk due to sepsis and vasopressor dependence, aligning with features like high Foley_sum, Sepsis3, and elevated vasopressor averages. The bias functions increase age, sepsis prevalence, and vasopressor doses to reflect severe sepsis cases.

bias_functions.notes: Increase age to reflect elderly population with higher sepsis risk.
Increase sepsis prevalence to reflect severe septic shock cases.
Increase norepinephrine dose to reflect severe vasopressor dependence.
Increase epinephrine dose to reflect severe shock requiring multiple vasopressors.
Increase Foley catheter use to reflect fluid monitoring in severe sepsis.
Increase organ dysfunction prevalence to reflect multi-organ failure.

targeted_profiles.sampling_notes: Ensure that generated samples reflect severe sepsis cases with high vasopressor requirements and multi-organ dysfunction. Avoid unrealistic combinations of extreme values.

targeted_profiles.title: Middle-Aged Obese Diabetic with Heart Failure
targeted_profiles.clinical_story: A 58-year-old obese female with type 2 diabetes and chronic heart failure presents with acute decompensated heart failure. She requires dobutamine infusion for inotropic support and develops acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy. Despite ICU interventions, she has a prolonged ICU stay and eventual in-hospital mortality.
targeted_profiles.why_this_profile: This profile targets patients with chronic comorbidities (obesity, diabetes, heart failure) who develop acute decompensation requiring inotropic support. The bias functions increase BMI, diabetes prevalence, and heart failure prevalence, while also increasing dobutamine use.

bias_functions.notes: Slightly increase age to reflect middle-aged population with chronic comorbidities.
Increase BMI to reflect obesity.
Increase diabetes prevalence to reflect high-risk diabetic population.
Increase heart failure prevalence to reflect chronic heart failure.
Increase dobutamine dose to reflect inotropic support.
Increase organ dysfunction prevalence to reflect acute kidney injury.

targeted_profiles.sampling_notes: Ensure that generated samples reflect obese diabetic patients with heart failure requiring inotropic support. Avoid unrealistic combinations of extreme values.

targeted_profiles.title: Young Trauma Patient with High Mortality Risk
targeted_profiles.clinical_story: A 25-year-old male involved in a motor vehicle collision presents with severe traumatic injuries including liver laceration and multiple rib fractures. He requires massive transfusion protocol and develops acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring prolonged mechanical ventilation. Despite aggressive ICU care, he develops multi-organ dysfunction and ultimately dies from hemorrhagic shock.
targeted_profiles.why_this_profile: This profile targets young trauma patients with high mortality risk due to hemorrhagic shock and multi-organ dysfunction. The bias functions increase trauma prevalence, anemia (due to blood loss), and organ dysfunction prevalence.

bias_functions.notes: Decrease age to reflect young trauma population.
Increase trauma prevalence to reflect severe traumatic injuries.
Increase anemia prevalence to reflect blood loss from trauma.
Increase organ dysfunction prevalence to reflect multi-organ failure.
Slightly increase Foley catheter use to reflect fluid monitoring in trauma.

targeted_profiles.sampling_notes: Ensure that generated samples reflect young trauma patients with severe injuries and high risk of multi-organ dysfunction. Avoid unrealistic combinations of extreme values.

targeted_profiles.title: Elderly with Advanced Cancer and ICU Admission
targeted_profiles.clinical_story: An 80-year-old female with metastatic lung cancer presents with acute respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation. She has a history of hypertension and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Despite ICU interventions, she develops septic shock from hospital-acquired pneumonia and ultimately dies from multi-organ failure.
targeted_profiles.why_this_profile: This profile targets elderly cancer patients with high mortality risk due to advanced disease and complications like septic shock. The bias functions increase age, cancer prevalence, and sepsis prevalence, while also increasing vasopressor use.

bias_functions.notes: Increase age to reflect elderly population with advanced cancer.
Increase cancer prevalence to reflect advanced cancer cases.
Increase sepsis prevalence to reflect hospital-acquired infections.
Increase norepinephrine dose to reflect septic shock.
Increase organ dysfunction prevalence to reflect multi-organ failure.

targeted_profiles.sampling_notes: Ensure that generated samples reflect elderly cancer patients with advanced disease and high risk of septic shock. Avoid unrealistic combinations of extreme values.

targeted_profiles.title: Post-Surgical Patient with Complications
targeted_profiles.clinical_story: A 65-year-old male undergoes major abdominal surgery for bowel obstruction. Post-operatively, he develops acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy and septic shock from anastomotic leak. Despite ICU interventions including high-dose vasopressors and antibiotics, he dies from multi-organ failure.
targeted_profiles.why_this_profile: This profile targets post-surgical patients with complications like acute kidney injury and septic shock. The bias functions increase surgical intervention prevalence (NSURG, TSURG), organ dysfunction, and sepsis prevalence.

bias_functions.notes: Increase non-trauma surgical intervention prevalence.
Increase trauma surgical intervention prevalence.
Increase organ dysfunction prevalence to reflect acute kidney injury.
Increase sepsis prevalence to reflect post-surgical infections.
Increase norepinephrine dose to reflect septic shock.

targeted_profiles.sampling_notes: Ensure that generated samples reflect post-surgical patients with complications like acute kidney injury and septic shock. Avoid unrealistic combinations of extreme values.

targeted_profiles.title: Young Obese Patient with Severe Anemia
targeted_profiles.clinical_story: A 30-year-old obese female with a history of menorrhagia presents with severe anemia (Hb 6.5 g/dL) and requires multiple blood transfusions. She develops acute heart failure from volume overload and requires ICU admission for close monitoring. Despite transfusions and diuresis, she develops acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and ultimately dies from multi-organ failure.
targeted_profiles.why_this_profile: This profile targets young obese patients with severe anemia and complications like heart failure and ARDS. The bias functions increase BMI, anemia prevalence, and heart failure prevalence.

bias_functions.notes: Decrease age to reflect young population.
Increase BMI to reflect obesity.
Increase anemia prevalence to reflect severe anemia cases.
Increase heart failure prevalence to reflect volume overload complications.
Increase organ dysfunction prevalence to reflect ARDS.

targeted_profiles.sampling_notes: Ensure that generated samples reflect young obese patients with severe anemia and complications like heart failure and ARDS. Avoid unrealistic combinations of extreme values.

targeted_profiles.title: Elderly with Chronic Liver Disease and Sepsis
targeted_profiles.clinical_story: An 82-year-old male with a history of cirrhosis presents with hepatic encephalopathy and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. He develops septic shock requiring high-dose vasopressors and develops acute kidney injury. Despite ICU interventions, he dies from multi-organ failure.
targeted_profiles.why_this_profile: This profile targets elderly patients with chronic liver disease and sepsis, a high-mortality combination. The bias functions increase age, liver disease prevalence, and sepsis prevalence, while also increasing vasopressor use and organ dysfunction.

bias_functions.notes: Increase age to reflect elderly population with chronic liver disease.
Increase liver disease prevalence to reflect cirrhosis cases.
Increase sepsis prevalence to reflect spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.
Increase norepinephrine dose to reflect septic shock.
Increase organ dysfunction prevalence to reflect acute kidney injury.

targeted_profiles.sampling_notes: Ensure that generated samples reflect elderly patients with chronic liver disease and sepsis. Avoid unrealistic combinations of extreme values.

targeted_profiles.title: Middle-Aged Patient with Immunosuppression and Pneumonia
targeted_profiles.clinical_story: A 50-year-old male with a history of rheumatoid arthritis on chronic steroids presents with severe community-acquired pneumonia requiring mechanical ventilation. He develops septic shock and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Despite ICU interventions including high-dose vasopressors and antibiotics, he dies from multi-organ failure.
targeted_profiles.why_this_profile: This profile targets immunosuppressed patients with severe infections like pneumonia. The bias functions increase immunosuppression prevalence, sepsis prevalence, and organ dysfunction prevalence.

bias_functions.notes: Slightly increase age to reflect middle-aged immunosuppressed population.
Increase immunosuppression prevalence to reflect chronic steroid use.
Increase sepsis prevalence to reflect severe pneumonia.
Increase organ dysfunction prevalence to reflect ARDS.
Increase norepinephrine dose to reflect septic shock.

targeted_profiles.sampling_notes: Ensure that generated samples reflect immunosuppressed patients with severe infections. Avoid unrealistic combinations of extreme values.

targeted_profiles.title: Elderly with Multiple Comorbidities and DNR Status
targeted_profiles.clinical_story: An 88-year-old female with a history of hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease presents with acute decompensated heart failure. She has a do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order and family requests comfort-focused care. Despite ICU admission for symptom management, she dies from cardiogenic shock.
targeted_profiles.why_this_profile: This profile targets elderly patients with multiple comorbidities and DNR status, reflecting end-of-life care. The bias functions increase age, comorbidity prevalence (diabetes, hypertension, heart failure, renal failure), and set DNR-related features.

bias_functions.notes: Increase age to reflect very elderly population.
Increase diabetes prevalence.
Increase hypertension prevalence.
Increase heart failure prevalence.
Increase renal failure prevalence.
Increase organ dysfunction prevalence to reflect cardiogenic shock.

targeted_profiles.sampling_notes: Ensure that generated samples reflect very elderly patients with multiple comorbidities and end-of-life care. Avoid unrealistic combinations of extreme values.

targeted_profiles.title: Young Patient with Acute Pancreatitis and Complications
targeted_profiles.clinical_story: A 28-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse presents with severe acute pancreatitis requiring ICU admission. He develops acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and septic shock from infected pancreatic necrosis. Despite ICU interventions including high-dose vasopressors and antibiotics, he dies from multi-organ failure.
targeted_profiles.why_this_profile: This profile targets young patients with severe acute pancreatitis and complications like ARDS and septic shock. The bias functions decrease age, increase organ dysfunction prevalence, and increase sepsis prevalence.

bias_functions.notes: Decrease age to reflect young population with alcohol-related pancreatitis.
Increase organ dysfunction prevalence to reflect ARDS and multi-organ failure.
Increase sepsis prevalence to reflect infected pancreatic necrosis.
Increase norepinephrine dose to reflect septic shock.
Slightly increase Foley catheter use to reflect fluid monitoring in pancreatitis.

targeted_profiles.sampling_notes: Ensure that generated samples reflect young patients with severe acute pancreatitis and complications. Avoid unrealistic combinations of extreme values.

causal_interaction_hypotheses.summary: The strongest pairwise interactions (e.g., Epinephrine_avg–Norepinephrine_avg) and SHAP-ranked features are correlational under a learned predictor and do not imply direct causal effects on in-hospital mortality. These patterns may reflect residual confounding, collider stratification, or label leakage via treatment–outcome feedback loops rather than mechanistic synergy or antagonism.

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Concomitant high exposure to both vasopressors may reflect refractory shock states where escalation of one agent necessitates addition of the other; the observed interaction could index severity rather than a direct pharmacologic interaction.
tying_evidence: diff-in-diff prediction -0.039 (quadrant a_high_b_high > a_high_b_low + a_low_b_high - a_low_b_low)
suggested_falsifiers: instrumental variable for vasopressor dosing
marginal structural model adjusting for time-varying confounders
physiologic trial randomizing epinephrine vs norepinephrine

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Higher urinary catheter burden and higher BMI may both be proxies for illness acuity and nursing workload; the interaction could reflect unmeasured severity or care intensity rather than a direct link between catheter use and mortality.
suggested_falsifiers: adjustment for SOFA score or APACHE II
analysis restricted to patients with similar catheter indications
randomized trial of early vs late catheterization

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Patients receiving epinephrine may be at higher risk of oliguria/anuria, prompting more aggressive fluid resuscitation and catheter placement; the interaction could capture hemodynamic instability rather than a direct catheter–mortality link.
suggested_falsifiers: stratified analysis by baseline creatinine
causal mediation analysis of urine output
physiologic trial of restrictive vs liberal fluids

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Norepinephrine-induced vasoconstriction may reduce renal perfusion pressure, leading to oliguria and increased catheter use; the interaction could reflect renal hypoperfusion rather than catheter-related harm.
suggested_falsifiers: analysis restricted to patients with normal baseline creatinine
instrumental variable for MAP during norepinephrine infusion
trial of renal-dose dopamine

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Age and BMI may jointly index frailty and metabolic reserve; the interaction could reflect cumulative physiologic stress rather than a direct age–BMI interaction on mortality.
tying_evidence: SHAP rank 2 for anchor_age, rank 3 for BMI
suggested_falsifiers: adjustment for frailty index
stratified analysis by functional status
longitudinal cohort with time-updated BMI

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Obese patients may have altered volume of distribution and drug clearance, potentially modulating the hemodynamic response to epinephrine; the interaction could reflect pharmacokinetic differences rather than direct pharmacologic synergy.
suggested_falsifiers: pharmacokinetic modeling of epinephrine clearance
trial of weight-based vs fixed-dose epinephrine
analysis stratified by BMI categories

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Hypertension and obesity often co-occur and share metabolic and vascular pathways; the interaction could reflect shared pathophysiology rather than a direct interaction on mortality.
tying_evidence: SHAP rank 11 for hypertension, rank 3 for BMI
suggested_falsifiers: mediation analysis of blood pressure control
genetic instrument for BMI and hypertension
randomized trial of lifestyle intervention

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Obesity may alter vascular responsiveness to norepinephrine, potentially modifying the risk of adverse outcomes; the interaction could reflect vascular physiology rather than direct drug effects.
suggested_falsifiers: vascular reactivity testing
trial of norepinephrine vs phenylephrine in obese patients
analysis stratified by endothelial function markers

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Older patients may have higher catheter utilization due to immobility, incontinence, or clinician preference; the interaction could reflect care patterns rather than catheter-related harm.
suggested_falsifiers: adjustment for ADL/IADL scores
analysis restricted to patients with similar catheter indications
randomized trial of early vs late catheterization in elderly

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Concomitant use of norepinephrine and neuromuscular blockers may reflect severe ARDS or refractory shock; the interaction could index illness severity rather than a direct pharmacologic interaction.
suggested_falsifiers: stratified analysis by ARDS status
causal mediation analysis of ventilator-free days
trial of early neuromuscular blockade

causal_hypotheses.narrative: Obesity may modulate the immune response to sepsis, potentially altering the risk of organ dysfunction and mortality; the interaction could reflect immunometabolic differences rather than direct BMI effects.
suggested_falsifiers: immunophenotyping in obese vs non-obese septic patients
trial of weight-adjusted sepsis bundles
genetic instrument for BMI
